A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show how a simple dynamic model of endogenous leverage and endogenous volatility can explain the pro-cyclical behavior of leverage, the pattern of implied volatilities, and the leverage requirements of different margin requirements.
, in the presence of heterogeneous beliefs, the leverage ratio of an asset can be pro-cyclical and the volatility of an asset is higher when the asset is traded at lower margin requirements.
, in a dynamic economy with endogenous leverage, bad news is more likely to increase future volatility and reduce leverage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a world with endogenous leverage, the relationship between first and seconds moments is ambiguous and depends on the nature of technology shocks.
the relationship between bad news and volatility is not a priori obvious and that the existing literature should not be taken for granted.
the interaction between leverage and volatility is not necessarily detrimental to the stability of the financial system.
